title: Solid-state conversion of heat to utility electricity

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a durable, manufacturable device that converts heat into electricity at utility scale, with system efficiency, power density, lifetime and cost competitive with a turbine-based alternative for a defined heat source. Its defining advance would be practical electricity generation without a turbine in the conversion stage. Achieving a high efficiency in one laboratory cell would establish an important component capability, but would not by itself establish this utility system.

Thermophotovoltaics provides the concrete route documented in the supplied evidence: a hot emitter supplies thermal radiation, and semiconductor cells convert suitable photons into electricity. Recovering photons below the semiconductor bandgap matters because those photons cannot produce the intended electrical output. The supplied review describes air-bridge cells designed to reflect much of this radiation, supporting efficient conversion at the cell level.

Scope synthesis: the broader concept also encompasses the thermionic and thermoelectric approaches named in the research. These are alternative conversion routes, not interchangeable descriptions of thermophotovoltaics. The supplied evidence evaluates a thermophotovoltaic result; it does not establish the present performance, deployment status or complete engineering barriers of the other approaches.

significance.text: If the proposed system performance were achieved, suitable thermal sources could supply electricity through modular conversion arrays without requiring a turbine for that conversion. The revolutionary consequence would be a new practical architecture for heat-based power generation, conditional on delivering competitive performance across the whole installation. The documented thermophotovoltaic mechanism grounds that possibility, and the authors identify thermal batteries as a potential application.

Application synthesis: coupling such a converter to stored high-temperature heat could make a thermal store an electricity-generating resource. Economical storage would remain a separate requirement: good conversion alone would not establish low storage cost, low standing losses, inexpensive charging or competitive electricity delivery. Concentrated solar heat and other thermal sources are further possibilities, provided their temperatures, heat-transfer arrangements and operating patterns suit the converter.

Impact limits: success for one high-temperature source would not establish replacement of combined-cycle gas turbines, compatibility with existing water-cooled nuclear plants or economical recovery of low-temperature waste heat. Each application needs its own source-matched efficiency, integration and cost assessment. For low-temperature recovery, thermodynamic limits depend on both hot- and cold-side absolute temperatures; a shrinking temperature difference alone does not establish a universal power-density limit or prove that a separate breakthrough is required. No specific historical ranking is warranted by the supplied material.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is integrated utility performance: a module and array that can be manufactured, operated and maintained while retaining competitive efficiency, power density, lifetime and cost. The supplied cell result does not demonstrate those properties together. Conversely, the limited evidence does not establish that no such system exists as of 1 November 2026; the unresolved breakthrough is the capability being sought, rather than a verified claim of worldwide absence.

For the documented thermophotovoltaic route, a concrete technical concern is managing the radiation spectrum. Photons below the bandgap cannot contribute to the intended electrical conversion, making their recovery important. The reported high reflectance addresses this concern at cell level. It does not by itself show how effectively a complete installation returns and reuses that radiation or what losses arise across an integrated emitter and converter array.

Engineering synthesis from the research: candidate barriers include electrical losses and series resistance, maintaining suitable emitter temperatures, scaling active area, managing heat removal, and preventing degradation over repeated operation. Manufacturing yield and consistent performance across many cells would also need examination. These are concrete issues for a development and validation program, but the supplied abstract does not establish their relative severity, show that every one remains unsolved, or justify applying the same barrier list to thermionic and thermoelectric systems.

System-assessment synthesis: the high-temperature emitter, cells, electrical connections, cooling and other supporting equipment must work together. A favorable cell measurement can coexist with substantial losses or costs elsewhere in the installation. Competitiveness therefore requires comparison against an alternative serving the same heat source and operating duty; the supplied evidence does not establish either that comparison or a general advantage over heat engines.

current_state.text: The supplied review identifies a journal result published on 17 July 2024: Roy-Layinde and colleagues, “High-efficiency air-bridge thermophotovoltaic cells,” Joule 8, pages 2135–2145, DOI 10.1016/j.joule.2024.05.002. The repository abstract reports up to 44 percent efficiency for single-junction InGaAs(P) air-bridge thermophotovoltaic cells under 1,435 °C blackbody illumination. It also reports 97–99 percent reflectance of below-bandgap photons across the stated semiconductor systems. These figures describe reported component performance under the specified illumination conditions.

The authors suggest thermal batteries among the potential applications. That application statement is a proposed use, not a demonstration of an integrated storage-and-generation plant. The supplied evidence does not establish megawatt output, sustained utility operation, installed cost or competitive net system efficiency. Nor does it support treating the 44 percent cell efficiency as the efficiency of a complete thermal battery or power plant.

The evidence available to the review was the repository abstract and bibliographic record, not the journal full text. Although the saved repository artifact was recorded as untruncated and without extraction issues, that does not make it a full-article assessment. Measurement procedures, uncertainty, detailed operating boundaries and independent replication were not assessed. The result should therefore be described as a reported journal cell result, rather than an independently verified record or the best result through 1 November 2026. This access limitation is not evidence that the reported result is false.

Evidence-bound assessment of deployment: the research asserted that a further search found no operating utility-scale thermophotovoltaic plant and that public projects remained planned or at pilot scale. The supplied review had no freshness-search record or supporting project descriptions with which to verify those assertions. Consequently, the current status of utility installations and integrated demonstrations remains unresolved in this record. The dated 2024 component result remains usable without resolving that broader deployment question.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: operate an integrated array delivering on the order of one megawatt continuously from a defined heat source for thousands of hours. Publish measured efficiency, output, installed cost and operating conditions, with an independent engineer or utility assessing competitiveness against a turbine-based alternative for the same source and duty. These are proposed demonstration thresholds, not established industry standards or achievements reported by the supplied source.
completion_criteria.label: Megawatt-scale array demonstrates competitive operation for thousands of continuous hours

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement boundary: define the heat input and electrical output consistently, distinguish gross from net electricity, account for auxiliary electricity consumption and cooling, and report relevant source and sink temperatures. State how recovered radiation enters the energy accounting. If thermal storage is included, report storage losses and charging requirements separately so that converter performance and complete storage-to-electricity performance can both be assessed.
completion_criteria.label: Define consistent heat-to-electricity measurement boundaries with complete energy accounting

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and durability evidence: disclose measurement methods and uncertainties, reproduce performance across multiple modules and manufacturing batches, and obtain independent assessment of representative operation. Track output degradation, thermal cycling, maintenance and replacement requirements. Thousands of operating hours would demonstrate sustained performance over that interval; it would not by itself establish an entire utility service life.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce performance across modules and manufacturing batches and document durability

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: identify the heat sources, temperature ranges, loads and environmental conditions for which the demonstration supports a competitive case. Establish manufacturing feasibility and cost assumptions at the intended deployment scale. Finite demonstrations establish breadth within tested conditions, not universal suitability for all thermal sources. A single cell exceeding 40 percent efficiency under a controlled emitter would remain a component milestone rather than completion of this system-level concept.
completion_criteria.label: Establish competitive operating boundaries and deployment-scale manufacturing feasibility

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — PWR-01, “Practical dissipationless conductors and windings for bulk power systems”: both concepts seek improved power-system hardware, and lower electrical losses could potentially benefit connections or supporting equipment in a conversion installation. PWR-01 concerns conductors and windings; PWR-02 concerns converting heat into electricity. Achieving either would not establish the other.

Roster-based synthesis — PWR-03, “Utility-scale electromagnetic delivery of power without a conductor”: both can involve electromagnetic energy, but the function differs. In the documented thermophotovoltaic route, thermal radiation supplies energy to a semiconductor converter. PWR-03 concerns delivering power without a conductor. Efficient conversion near a hot emitter would not establish practical utility-scale wireless delivery.

Roster-based synthesis — PWR-04, “Site-independent storage from multi-day weather through seasonal imbalance”: thermal storage is a possible connection because PWR-02 could provide its electricity-generation stage. PWR-04 additionally requires suitable storage duration, capacity, losses, economics and site independence. A successful converter would not establish those storage properties, and a successful store would not establish competitive heat-to-electric conversion.

Roster-based synthesis — PWR-05, “An interconnection that no longer depends on synchronous machines”: turbine-free conversion could be relevant to a power system with fewer rotating generators, but production of electricity and stable grid operation are separate capabilities. PWR-02 would still require an appropriate grid interface. It would not by itself demonstrate the control, stability and interconnection capabilities implied by PWR-05.

change_log.change: Preserved PWR-02 and its title while making competitive integrated utility conversion the central capability.
change_log.reason: The concept remains meaningful even though the supplied evidence establishes a component result rather than a complete power system.

change_log.change: Retained the 44 percent efficiency, 1,435 °C illumination temperature, 97–99 percent reflectance range and 17 July 2024 publication date, with component-level scope.
change_log.reason: The review supports these reported quantities through the repository abstract, but does not support interpreting them as plant performance.

change_log.change: Replaced “best verified” and the asserted absence of utility plants with explicit limits on ranking and deployment knowledge.
change_log.reason: Full measurement assessment and a documented freshness search were not supplied; missing evidence neither establishes absence nor invalidates the dated result.

change_log.change: Preserved series resistance, emitter temperature, scaling and degradation as qualified engineering concerns.
change_log.reason: These useful research details inform the development problem, but the abstract does not establish a complete or ranked list of unsolved barriers.

change_log.change: Separated thermophotovoltaic evidence from the broader thermionic and thermoelectric scope.
change_log.reason: The supplied source does not establish comparable results or identical barriers for those alternative routes.

change_log.change: Qualified source-specific applications and removed unsupported prevalence, incumbent-efficiency and conventional-steam temperature comparisons.
change_log.reason: The conditional benefits remain useful, but the supplied evidence does not substantiate the broader comparisons.

change_log.change: Reframed low-temperature recovery around specified hot- and cold-side conditions rather than a categorical further-breakthrough claim.
change_log.reason: Temperature difference alone does not establish practical power density or a universal feasibility boundary.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed megawatt demonstration with measurement boundaries, reproducibility, degradation and source-matched comparison.
change_log.reason: These make the system target assessable while preserving that the thresholds are proposals and finite operation does not establish lifetime or universal applicability.

change_log.change: Explained overlaps and distinctions with all four other roster entries.
change_log.reason: Connections to conductors, wireless delivery, storage and grid operation should remain visible without merging separate innovations.

unresolved_issues: The full article's measurement methods, uncertainty analysis, operating boundaries and replication evidence were not assessed in the supplied review.
Whether the 2024 result remains a leading result through 1 November 2026 is unresolved.
Operating utility-scale installations, pilot status and planned integrated demonstrations cannot be established without the missing freshness-search record and project evidence.
The severity and present resolution of the proposed engineering barriers, including those for thermionic and thermoelectric alternatives, remain unestablished by the supplied source.
Competitive net efficiency, power density, installed cost and service life for a defined heat source remain to be demonstrated or documented.
Application-specific suitability for concentrated solar heat, existing water-cooled nuclear plants, combined-cycle replacement and low-temperature waste heat remains unresolved.

brief.title: Power plant electricity from heat without turbines
possible: Communities and industry could get electricity from heat through arrays of devices instead of turbines. The goal is a complete power system that can match a turbine alternative on efficiency, output for its size, working life and cost.

Stored heat could become a source of electricity when needed. One route uses cells that turn light from a hot surface into electrical power, while reflecting unusable light back to keep the surface hot.
why: Power producers would gain another way to build heat-based generating plants, using modular arrays. Coupling these converters to heat storage could also give electricity suppliers another way to deliver stored energy.

sources.showed: Their heat-to-electricity cells reflected most of the light they could not convert, reducing energy lost at the cell.
sources.quote: Air-bridge TPVs have demonstrated enhanced power conversion efficiencies by recuperating a large amount of power carried by below-band-gap (out-of-band) photons.
sources.cited_for: Reflecting unusable light can improve conversion at the cell.
sources.not_established: A complete plant still needs to demonstrate competitive performance, cost and durability.

sources.showed: Antora reported building a pilot production line for heat-to-electricity cells and qualifying a manufacturing supply chain.
sources.quote:
We have scaled up our equipment and processes to a production line with a 2 MW/year 
capacity
sources.cited_for: Cell manufacturing has progressed beyond individual laboratory devices.
sources.not_established: Production capacity does not establish the output, efficiency or economics of an operating power plant.

sources.who: Masahiro Suemitsu, Takashi Asano, Takuya Inoue and Susumu Noda
sources.showed: The researchers reported a small heat-to-electricity system with 11.2% efficiency, measuring heat input and electrical output directly.
sources.quote:
With this we 
experimentally obtain 𝜂system_exp = 11.2%
sources.cited_for: Direct heat-input measurements can establish efficiency beyond the cell alone.
sources.not_established: The small experiment did not establish utility-scale output, sustained operation or competitive cost.

sources.who: Esther López, Irene Artacho and Alejandro Datas
sources.showed: The researchers measured conversion with the hot surface close to the cell, capturing repeated reflections and the effects of higher electrical output per area.
sources.quote:
Importantly, we show that the  use of high VFs results in much  higher power densities 
when compared to previous results reported in the literature.
sources.cited_for: The arrangement of the hot surface and cell affects meaningful efficiency measurements.
sources.not_established: A laboratory measurement does not establish complete plant efficiency or operating life.

sources.who: Alina LaPotin and colleagues at MIT and NREL
sources.showed: The researchers built cells with stacked electricity-generating layers and measured electrical output alongside heat dissipated by the cells.
sources.quote: Here we report TPV efficiency measurements of > 40% , measured directly through calorimetry.
sources.cited_for: Cells can achieve high conversion efficiency under controlled heating.
sources.not_established: Cell efficiency does not establish the efficiency or cost of a complete storage-and-generation system.

shown: Roy-Layinde and colleagues reported cell efficiency of up to 44% under controlled illumination from a very hot source. This is a component result, rather than the efficiency of an entire power plant.

Antora reported a cell production line with capacity equivalent to 2 megawatts of generating equipment per year. That is manufacturing progress; it is not a demonstration of continuous electricity generation at that scale.
missing: An integrated array still needs to demonstrate competitive efficiency, output, cost and durability together for a defined heat source.
Complete energy accounting must include cooling, supporting equipment and losses as reflected light returns to the hot surface.
Consistent manufacturing and repeated operation must establish maintenance needs, replacement rates and degradation.

milestones.label: A megawatt array runs competitively for thousands of hours
milestones.explanation: An integrated array would have to sustain output with independently assessed efficiency, installed cost and operating conditions. This would establish competitiveness against a turbine serving the same heat source and duty.

milestones.label: Complete energy accounting makes efficiency comparisons meaningful
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to account consistently for heat input, usable electricity, cooling, supporting equipment and recovered light, with storage losses separate. This would distinguish converter performance from whole-system performance.

milestones.label: Manufactured modules reproduce performance and withstand repeated operation
milestones.explanation: Modules from different production batches would have to reproduce results with stated uncertainties and independent assessment, while tracking wear and maintenance. This would test whether performance survives manufacturing and use.

milestones.label: Competitive uses and manufacturing feasibility are established
milestones.explanation: Testing would have to identify suitable heat sources and operating conditions, alongside credible manufacturing costs at deployment scale. This would define where a practical competitive case holds.

uncertain: Which heat sources and operating temperatures can support a competitive complete system?
How severe will cooling, electrical losses and material degradation become as arrays grow?
How well will sustained demonstrations predict a full utility service life?
